items.t: Meta Pressed by Democrats to Address Concerns Over AI Glasses
items.d: A pair of Senate Democrats are looking into potential privacy and safety risks associated with Meta’s smart glasses amid rising concerns about the devices’ usage for non-consensual recordings and data collection that trains AI systems.

items.t: Driverless Trucks Can Double Profits, Says Aurora CEO
items.d: Driverless trucking company Aurora is ramping up production and switching to a ‘driver-as-a-service model’ as it looks to reach profitability and meet demand. Aurora co-founder and CEO Chris Urmson discusses how the company is scaling and what he sees as a friendly regulatory environment amid a national truck-driving shortage. Urmson joins Ed Ludlow on “Bloomberg Tech.” (Source: Bloomberg)

items.t: Bluesky blocks links to leaked DHS employee data as government seeks takedowns
items.d: The social networking site is facing criticism for blocking access to the site, which identifies thousands of ICE agents and other employees working for Homeland Security.
items.fullText: Following a sizable leak of personnel data about employees who work for the U.S. Department of Homeland Security, social network Bluesky is now blocking its users from accessing a nonprofit’s website that hosts the leaked dataset. Users reported that the links to nonprofit transparency collective DDoSecrets were marked as “malicious” soon after TechCrunch and other media outlets broke the news that Homeland Security had been hacked. A screenshot showing Bluesky blocking links to DDoSecrets Image Credits: TechCrunch TechCrunch reported on Wednesday that a hacker obtained over 40,000 user account records from Homeland Security’s login system, including the names and contact information, such as work-issued phone numbers and email addresses, of employees and agents working for its various agencies like Customs and Border Protection (CBP) and Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). The data included information that was similar to that on an employee’s business card. DDoSecrets, which publishes leaked datasets in the public interest, also made the hacked data publicly available. Researchers who are investigating abuses by the Trump administration say that the data will be invaluable for seeking records from the government under public records laws. A spokesperson for Homeland Security told TechCrunch on Wednesday that it was “aware of a potential breach and is actively working to address the situation swiftly and effectively.” In a statement, Bluesky chief operating officer Rose Wang told TechCrunch: “Our Community Guidelines protect people’s safety and privacy by prohibiting the unauthorized sharing of personal information and other content that could pose safety risks. items.t: Who will you learn from in 6 days at TechCrunch Founder Summit? Meet the founders and investors taking the stages
items.d: Six days from now, on November 4, TechCrunch Founder Summit brings experienced founders, investors, and operators to Boston to share the decisions, mistakes, pivots, and lessons that shaped their companies. Register before it starts for ticket savings and deals.
items.fullText: There are plenty of places to find startup advice. TechCrunch Founder Summit is about hearing what happened when people actually put that advice to the test. Six days from now, TechCrunch Founder Summit , presented by Fidelity Private Shares , brings experienced founders, investors, and operators to Boston to share the decisions, mistakes, pivots, and lessons that shaped their companies. Register now to save up to $100 , get a second ticket free when you buy one, or save up to 30% on group ticket bundles. Don’t miss these deals before the event starts on November 4. Who and what are on the agenda Explore the full Founder Summit agenda to discover the breakout and roundtable sessions and speakers bringing actionable insights, hard-earned lessons, and practical advice to help you scale your startup. Image Credits: Halo Creative / Flickr (opens in a new window) From Boston startup to public company Few stories capture the potential of the Boston startup ecosystem better than Toast . Steve Fredette , president, co-founder, and director of Toast, will talk about what it takes to keep reinventing a company even after the original idea works. Scaling creates a new set of questions: How do you keep innovating? How do you stay close to the customers who got you there? And how do you evolve as technology and expectations change around you? For founders trying to move from early traction toward meaningful scale, those are the questions that matter. Know whether you’re actually ready to grow Growth can be exciting. Premature growth can be expensive. Kent Bennett , partner at Bessemer Venture Partners , will explore how founders can recognize meaningful product-market fit before they scale. items.fullText: Pioneers Across Europe Deploy NVIDIA Earth-2 Open Models to Power Real-World Weather and Climate Prediction October 21, 2026 by Niall Robinson 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Weather forecasts shape more than daily plans; timely weather information is crucial for energy producers, insurers and transport operators to plan around changing conditions. A global forecast can show a storm taking shape, but decisions about solar farms, shipping routes or insured property depend on what happens locally. NVIDIA Earth-2 gives developers and researchers a family of open AI models and tools they can customize with their own data. Running on NVIDIA computing, these technologies support global weather prediction, detailed regional forecasts and environmental research. Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements StormScope EU is the latest model to join Earth-2 — a regional version of the StormScope model for short-term forecasting, trained over Europe weather and climate data. It uses EUMETSAT satellite observations to predict evolving cloud conditions across 16 Meteosat channels at 10-minute intervals. At GTC Berlin, NVIDIA is showcasing a live StormScope EU pipeline in an interactive weather demo built in partnership with Earthmover . The demo uses Earth2Studio to run forecasts and Earthmover’s data platform to manage and serve the real-time results, which are updated as soon as new satellite observations come in, every 10 minutes. Earthmover serves these results as map tiles, letting visitors explore predictions across Europe without downloading entire datasets. Developers can combine Earth-2 models in workflows tailored to regional needs, using StormScope for short-term forecasting and CorrDiff to add local detail to coarser weather data.
